frequency_question: How often do targeted highly-controversial federal voter eligibility bills successfully pass at least one chamber of Congress under unified or divided government within a given two-year legislative session?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly titled voter eligibility or proof-of-citizenship election integrity bills; excludes general omnibus spending bills, routine election administration updates, or non-binding resolutions.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act Amendments (REAL ID related iterations)

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 10 major tracked legislative pushes across the last decade; 3 passed at least one chamber.
known_gaps: Minor subcommittee-only bills that never reached floor debate are excluded.
skeleton: Total high-profile partisan voter verification bills introduced across 10 congressional sessions since 2005, partitioned by whether they achieved floor passage in the originating legislative chamber.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 10 major legislative pushes achieving floor passage in at least one chamber under varying partisan alignments.
validity_reason: Valid through the end of the current congressional baseline structure; expires with major structural shifts in congressional procedure or major electoral reform overhauls.
